content:
Over the past year, we've been eagerly anticipating an iPad mini update, and it seems the wait may soon be over. Last week's scoop from Aaron Perris revealed that the new device is expected to feature an A20 Pro chip and narrower bezels, and we've learned it will sport an OLED display with waterproofing.

While these upgrades are certainly appealing, I have one main hope for the next iPad mini — and it has nothing to do with hardware, but rather software.

After seeing the iPhone Duo, I was impressed by how Apple handled multitasking on that device. Multitasking on the iPad has always been a mess for me, but the experience on the iPhone Duo was effortlessly elegant.

Performing proper windowing on such a small screen has never quite made sense on the iPad mini. Users rarely stack multiple windows on the iPad mini either. So I hope Apple will take a cue from the iPhone Duo: add split-screen plus picture-in-picture functionality.

Honestly, that experience was fantastic. Currently on the iPad mini, in portrait mode you simply can't pull a picture-in-picture window to take up the full width of the device, and even if you could, you'd either be covering part of the app or having to manually resize the window.

Bringing split video and app viewing to the iPad mini's screen seems like a no-brainer to me, especially considering the iPhone Duo and iPad mini share similar screen aspect ratios. At least for myself, if this feature existed, I'd use portrait mode on the iPad mini far more often.
